messages:
Marta (Support): customer reported a huge dedicated commit charge overnight for rp-us-9 but only ~30 tokens served in that period. invoice shows 14.8 reserved hours.
Diego (Billing): ping pool id + invoice line please. need to know if this looks like production traffic or infra attribution.
Marta (Support): pool=rp-us-9, commit=cmt-9901, invoice: "Dedicated Reserved Hours — 14.8h — $185.60". customer attached app logs: almost zero requests 01:20–02:50 UTC.
Hannah (SRE): grabbing metering and router logs. initial glance: many alloc.create events labelled reason=burst and reason=prewarm between 01:18 and 02:46. user request count is negligible.
metering-bot: alloc events excerpt:
```
2026-05-11T01:18:02Z alloc/create id=alloc-1501 reason=burst warmup=true
2026-05-11T01:20:12Z alloc/create id=alloc-1502 reason=prewarm warmup=true
2026-05-11T02:46:22Z alloc/destroy id=alloc-1501 duration=01:28:20 billed_hours=1.47
2026-05-11T02:46:30Z alloc/destroy id=alloc-1502 duration=01:26:18 billed_hours=1.44
```
Vik (Infra): router traces show probe clients hitting pool rp-us-9 with a special test-client header x-int-test=true starting 01:17:58. That header shouldn't be present on customer pools — looks like an internal test ran against the wrong tenant.
internal-test-bot: Scheduled stress test run test-suite:burst-2026-05-11 targeting pool_selector: tag=smoke-tests
Marta (Support): customer says they didn't run any scheduled tests. they rotated keys yesterday but that was earlier in the evening.
Hannah (SRE): digging deeper: the allocator attribution service maps incoming requests to pools. I see a mapping edge-case where requests with header x-int-test=true and missing tenant-id fall back to the default pool resolver. Our default resolver for that org points to rp-us-9 due to an old dev override. So two issues: misrouted internal test traffic + prewarm probes left running.
Diego (Billing): so internal load test traffic plus warmup allocations were billed to the customer's commit? that would explain the hours. can we produce an evidence bundle for finance and the customer?
Lena (Finance): yes please include: alloc ids, billed hours, API request counts, probe headers, and the internal test schedule. we'll open an adj hold once we have proof.
Hannah (SRE): evidence bundle collected: alloc ids [alloc-1501, alloc-1502, alloc-1509, alloc-1510], billed_hours [1.47,1.44,2.1,2.3], api_request_count for pool rp-us-9 in window=12 (all from internal-test-bot), router headers show x-int-test=true, tenant-id header absent in those requests. Also found prewarm-controller config: keepalive=600s which kept instances alive after probe success.
Vik (Infra): quick router snippet:
````
[01:18:00Z] src=10.40.12.8 -> router pool=rp-us-9 headers=[x-int-test=true, missing tenant-id]
[01:18:00Z] router -> alloc create id=alloc-1501
````
Marta (Support): customer is asking for immediate credit and to not be charged for non-customer traffic.
Diego (Billing): propose refund criteria: any alloc billed to a committed pool where api_request_count from the pool owner == 0 and all requests attributed to internal-test-bot. I'll draft ADJ template.
Lena (Finance): opened adj ticket ADJ-9021 for cmt-9901, putting invoice on hold pending SRE verification. please attach the SRE bundle.
Hannah (SRE): root cause summary: internal stress test invoked against wrong target due to fallback resolver when tenant-id header missing; attribution bug plus long prewarm keepalive amplified billed hours.
Marta (Support): what mitigations are we pushing? customer wants assurance this won't happen again.
Hannah (SRE): mitigations lined up:
- change default resolver to return explicit 4xx when tenant-id missing (no fallback to customer pools)
- add strict segregation for internal-test-bot IPs so they never map to customer commits
- reduce prewarm-controller.keepalive from 600s -> 60s for committed pools
- add dedicated telemetry to alert on allocs with header x-int-test or missing tenant-id -> ReservedPoolMisattribution alert
Vik (Infra): I'll roll the resolver change and the keepalive update to canary immediately and add an Nginx rule to drop any requests with x-int-test true from mapping to customer pools. deploy-bot queued the change.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: resolver-config v2026.05.11-rc2 -> canary
Diego (Billing): once SRE confirms the bundle and fixes, propose full credit for all billed_hours from allocs in the bundle and a written confirmation to the customer.
Lena (Finance): agree; will prepare credit memo after confirmation.
Hannah (SRE): monitoring will watch rp-us-9 for 24h. created incident tracker IT-3384 for this misrouting and set owner.
Marta (Support): notified customer with interim findings and promised rollback/credit ETA 48h. customer acknowledged, asked only that we keep them updated.
Hannah (SRE): FINAL_NOTE: root cause = internal test misrouted + attribution fallback + long prewarm keepalive. mitigations deployed to canary. evidence bundle uploaded to ADJ-9021. follow-up in 6h to confirm no repeat billing.
Marta (Support): closing loop for now, will update thread when finance posts the credit. :white_check_mark:
